candidates.summary: Norwegian police and the PST security service said they were investigating telecommunications company Telenor on suspicion of aiding crimes against humanity in Myanmar and violating sanctions. Investigators raided Telenor’s Oslo headquarters on Tuesday. Telenor said it was cooperating and argued that employees in Myanmar had faced severe risks if they did not comply with military orders. No individuals had been charged or placed under investigation.
candidates.title: Norwegian police raid Telenor headquarters in Myanmar-related investigation

candidates.summary: United Nations officials said the Ebola epidemic in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remained large and was still growing in some areas, although containment efforts were showing progress elsewhere. Government figures published Tuesday listed 7,258 confirmed cases and 3,510 deaths across seven provinces. WHO official Olivier le Polain said it was too early to conclude that the outbreak had passed its peak.
candidates.title: UN says eastern Congo Ebola outbreak remains extensive despite some progress

candidates.summary: U.S. presidential envoy John Coale met Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko for their first talks in six months. Washington has sought additional prisoner releases in exchange for sanctions relief. Belarusian state media said Coale conveyed President Donald Trump’s support for the negotiations. Human-rights group Viasna says Belarus still holds more than 900 political prisoners; Lukashenko rejects that characterization.
candidates.title: US envoy meets Lukashenko for renewed prisoner-release talks

candidates.summary: Ukraine’s Brigadier-General Andrii Biletskyi announced an offensive operation named Vivaldi in northern Donetsk region. He said Ukrainian forces had cleared Russian infiltration groups from 75 square kilometers, recaptured another 10 square kilometers and taken control of several villages or surrounding areas. Reuters said it could not independently verify the territorial claims.
candidates.title: Ukrainian commander announces offensive operation in northern Donetsk

candidates.summary: Rail services across central and northern Netherlands were disrupted during Tuesday’s morning rush after pipes were deliberately attached to tracks at about 20 locations, infrastructure operator ProRail said. Several road level crossings also remained closed. ProRail described the incidents as deliberate human-caused disruption but said the responsible party and motive were unknown; national police opened an investigation.
candidates.title: Deliberately placed pipes disrupt Dutch rail network

candidates.summary: Independent United Nations experts reported that Belarusian courts, police, security services, prosecutors and prison authorities had acted in a coordinated manner to repress government critics throughout the justice process. The panel cited arbitrary arrests, torture, denial of legal safeguards, closed trials and harassment after release. Belarus has previously rejected UN criticism and did not immediately respond to the new findings.
candidates.title: UN experts report systematic justice-system abuses in Belarus

priorStories.headline: Houthis capture two Red Sea islands
priorStories.body:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels took control of the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands after government-allied forces withdrew, according to two Yemeni government officials and a Houthi official.

The islands are in the southern Red Sea, about 160 kilometers north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a major shipping route.

priorStories.headline: Israeli strikes in Lebanon kill 13
priorStories.body:
Israeli strikes on a town in southern Lebanon killed at least 13 people, including six children, according to Lebanon’s Health Ministry.

The attacks came during several days of escalating strikes despite a ceasefire reached by Israel and Hezbollah in June.

priorStories.headline: Saudi oil pipeline faces weeks of repairs
priorStories.body:
Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline is expected to remain mostly out of service for three to five weeks after an attack last week damaged the line and a major pumping facility, two regional officials briefed on repairs said.

One official said limited oil movements might continue while repairs are underway.

priorStories.headline: Supreme Court keeps mail-ballot rules unchanged
priorStories.body:
The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s emergency request to permit new restrictions on mail ballots before November’s midterm elections.

The brief order said the administration was unlikely to prevail in court. Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas publicly dissented. Existing state mail-ballot processes remain in effect while the litigation continues.
